indication_label: Duchenne muscular dystrophy, all patients 4 years and older (label June 2024 to November 2025, ambulatory and non-ambulatory); base prevalence, males aged 5-24
unit: DMD cases per 10,000 males aged 5-24 (point prevalence, 2010); DBMD combined 1.38
verbatim: In 2010, prevalence of DBMD was 1.38 per 10 000 male individuals, ages 5 to 24 years.
source_doc: Romitti PA, Zhu Y, Puzhankara S, et al. Prevalence of Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies in the United States. Pediatrics 2015;135(3):513-521 (MD STARnet, 6 US sites)
notes: Abstract read via Europe PMC; phenotype split read in the PMC full text: DMD 1.02 and BMD 0.36 per 10,000 males aged 5-24 in 2010; 543 of 765 definite/probable cases (71%) were DMD. Denominator 3,827,532 males aged 5-24 across the 6 sites. Only US population-based DMD prevalence available; CDC data pages (cdc.gov/muscular-dystrophy) blocked to fetch.

indication_label: Duchenne muscular dystrophy, prevalent US males aged 5-24 (proxy for the 4-and-older label pool)
verbatim: In 2010, prevalence of DBMD was 1.38 per 10 000 male individuals, ages 5 to 24 years.
source_doc: Derived from Romitti 2015 (MD STARnet) prevalence and US Census Bureau Vintage 2024 national population estimates by single year of age and sex (NC-EST2024-AGESEX-RES)
notes: Arithmetic: US males aged 5-24 on 1 July 2024 = 43,934,374 (Census file, SEX=1, ages 5-24 summed). Low = 1.02/10,000 x 43,934,374 = 4,481 (DMD phenotype only). High = 1.38/10,000 x 43,934,374 = 6,063 (DMD+BMD; Becker is not an Elevidys indication so this is an upper bound). Excludes 4-year-olds (about 1/20 of the 5-24 cohort, roughly +220) and adults 25+ (small, poorly counted). Prevalence is 2010 vintage; corticosteroid and ventilation use have lengthened survival since, so the true 4+ pool is probably somewhat larger.

indication_label: People living with Duchenne in the United States (advocacy estimate, all ages)
unit: prevalent pool (people living with Duchenne, all ages, approximate)
verbatim: According to Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy, around 15,000 young men and a small number of young women are currently living with Duchenne in the United States.
source_doc: Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy, About Duchenne (web page, accessed 5 Sep 2026)
notes: Same page: "Duchenne muscular dystrophy affects approximately 1 in every 5,000 boys, with an estimated 20,000 children born with the condition worldwide each year." The 15,000 figure is 2.5-3x the MD STARnet-based 5-24 pool (4,481-6,063); treat 15,000 as an all-ages upper bound and the MD STARnet figure as a lower bound.

indication_label: DMD birth incidence, US (MDA)
verbatim: DMD occurs in approximately 1 in 3,500 to 5,000 male births.
source_doc: Muscular Dystrophy Association, Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) disease page (accessed 5 Sep 2026)
notes: MDA page cites Romitti 2015 as its source. Applied to 1,846,708 US male births/age-0 males (Census Vintage 2024) this gives 369-528 DMD births per year, consistent with the existing E3a derived row (364-557).

indication_label: DMD point prevalence and birth prevalence, systematic review (USA point prevalence)
unit: DMD cases per 100,000 males (point prevalence, USA study in review); birth prevalence 15.9-19.5 per 100,000 live births
verbatim: Birth prevalence ranged from 15.9 to 19.5 per 100,000 live births. Point prevalence per 100,000 males was for France, USA, UK and Canada, 10.9, 1.9, 2.2 and 6.1 respectively. ... Loss of ambulation occurred at a median age of 12 and ventilation starts at about 20 years.
source_doc: Ryder S, Leadley RM, Armstrong N, et al. The burden, epidemiology, costs and treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: an evidence review. Orphanet J Rare Dis 2017;12:79
notes: Abstract read via Europe PMC REST (PMID 28446219, PMC5405509); the publisher page redirects to a Springer login. The 1.9 per 100,000 US figure is an all-male-ages point prevalence and is far below MD STARnet 5-24 (10.2 per 100,000); the review itself flags evidence gaps in prevalence. Median loss of ambulation at 12 years is the key input for the ambulatory/non-ambulatory split.

indication_label: Share of US males with Duchenne (under 35) who are ambulatory (Duchenne Registry, 2007-2016)
verbatim: Among males with Duchenne, mean age (SD) was 11.3 (6.5) years, the majority (88.9%) were less than 20 years old and Caucasian (87.2%), and most individuals were ambulatory (59.3%), with 40.0% nonambulatory. The mean age (SD) of onset for full-time use of a scooter/wheelchair was 10.8 (2.5) years.
source_doc: Cowen L, Mancini M, Martin A, Lucas A, Donovan JM. Variability and trends in corticosteroid use by male United States participants with Duchenne muscular dystrophy in the Duchenne Registry. BMC Neurology 2019;19:84
notes: Table 1: ambulatory 892 (59.3%), nonambulatory 602 (40.0%), infant not yet walking 11 (0.7%) of 1,505 US males with Duchenne under 35 (self/parent-reported, PPMD registry). Registry skews young (mean age 11.3) so the ambulatory share of the true 4+ population is probably lower than 59%. Best US split found; no Sarepta statement of the ambulatory share was located.

indication_label: Share of US males with Duchenne (under 35) who are non-ambulatory (Duchenne Registry, 2007-2016)
verbatim: Nonambulatory Use a wheelchair/other mobility device and rarely/ never walk 602 (40.0)
source_doc: Cowen L, Mancini M, Martin A, Lucas A, Donovan JM. Variability and trends in corticosteroid use by male United States participants with Duchenne muscular dystrophy in the Duchenne Registry. BMC Neurology 2019;19:84
notes: Table 1 of the paper. Non-ambulatory patients were covered by the Elevidys label only from June 2024 to November 2025 (accelerated approval, removed from Indications after two ALF deaths; shipments to non-ambulatory patients suspended from June 2025).

indication_label: Ambulatory DMD patients aged 4 and older, US (label from June 2024 and again from November 2025)
verbatim: most individuals were ambulatory (59.3%), with 40.0% nonambulatory
source_doc: Derived from Romitti 2015 x Census 2024 (this file), PPMD ~15,000 (this file) and the Duchenne Registry ambulatory share (Cowen 2019)
notes: Arithmetic: 59.3% x 4,481 (MD STARnet DMD-only, males 5-24) = 2,657 (low); 59.3% x 6,063 (DBMD upper bound) = 3,595 (mid); 59.3% x 15,000 (PPMD all-ages) = 8,895 (high). Before anti-AAVrh74 antibody screening (titre >= 1:400 excluded) and prior-treatment attrition. The existing E3a provisional row (80% of the addressable ambulatory population untreated, Sarepta CEO) is consistent with a pool in the low thousands.

indication_label: Non-ambulatory DMD patients aged 4 and older, US (label June 2024 to November 2025 only)
verbatim: most individuals were ambulatory (59.3%), with 40.0% nonambulatory
source_doc: Derived from Romitti 2015 x Census 2024 (this file), PPMD ~15,000 (this file) and the Duchenne Registry non-ambulatory share (Cowen 2019)
notes: Arithmetic: 40.0% x 4,481 = 1,792 (low); 40.0% x 6,063 = 2,425 (mid); 40.0% x 15,000 = 6,000 (high). DMD_4plus_all = amb + nonamb: 4,481-15,000. Registry under-represents adults, so the non-ambulatory share of the real population is likely above 40%.

indication_label: Sarepta statement of the US addressable Elevidys population after the June 2024 label expansion
verbatim: ELEVIDYS received traditional approval by the FDA in June 2024 for the treatment of ambulatory patients at least four years old with Duchenne with a confirmed mutation in the Duchenne gene. ELEVIDYS was also approved for non-ambulatory patients under the accelerated approval pathway in June 2024.
source_doc: Sarepta Therapeutics Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2 Mar 2026); Sarepta 8-K Ex-99.1 earnings releases of 13 Jan 2025, 26 Feb 2025, 3 Nov 2025 and 25 Feb 2026 (all full-text grepped)
notes: None of the Sarepta SEC filings state a US DMD patient count or an addressable-population figure for Elevidys (the 10-K gives prevalent populations only for FSHD ~13,000 and DM1 ~30,000). SEC full-text search for "Duchenne" + "addressable" in Sarepta 8-Ks 2024-2026 returned 0 hits. Sarepta IR site (investorrelations.sarepta.com), BioSpace and BusinessWire were unreachable from this environment (curl wrote nothing; WebFetch timed out/empty). A search summary attributed "DMD population estimated at around 14,000, including ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients" to BioSpace coverage of the June 2024 approval, but the page could not be opened, so it is not recorded as a value.

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor (US accelerated approval, March 2024)
verbatim: The FDA granted accelerated approval of Breyanzi for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma who have received at least two prior lines of therapy, including a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor and a B-cell lymphoma 2 inhibitor.
source_doc: BMS 8-K Ex-99.1 Q1-2024 earnings release (25 Apr 2024); BMS ASCO 2024 Breyanzi release boilerplate (news.bms.com); BusinessWire approval release (403); Europe PMC search for US double-exposed CLL population estimates
notes: No BMS statement of a US eligible count was found; BMS boilerplate gives no CLL incidence. ICER has not reviewed Breyanzi in CLL. No G-BA procedure exists for liso-cel in CLL (G-BA lists only LBCL 3L D-867, LBCL 2L D-951 and FL 3L D-1196), so no German count either. Europe PMC query for US real-world double-exposed/double-refractory CLL population estimates returned nothing usable. Existing E1a denominator: ~22,760 new CLL cases per year (ACS).

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy (US accelerated approval, May 2024)
verbatim: FL is the second most common form of NHL and the most common subtype of indolent NHL, accounting for 20 to 30 percent of all NHL cases.
source_doc: BMS Breyanzi ASCO 2024 press release boilerplate (news.bms.com, 2024); BMS Q1-2024 8-K; Europe PMC
notes: No US 3L+ FL flow found from BMS, ICER or NICE (NICE has no liso-cel FL appraisal; TA1159 covers 3L LBCL). Germany figure of 370-840 GKV patients per year (this file) can be scaled: Germany GKV ~74m insured vs US ~340m population implies roughly 1,700-3,900 per year in the US if treatment patterns were identical (not recorded as a value; population-scaling across systems is unreliable).

indication_label: Relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor (US accelerated approval, May 2024)
verbatim: MCL is an aggressive, rare form of NHL, representing roughly 3% of all NHL cases.
source_doc: BMS Breyanzi ASCO 2024 press release boilerplate; BMS Q1-2024 8-K; Europe PMC search for US post-BTKi MCL treatment-pattern studies
notes: No US count located. Europe PMC returned only a BTKi adherence study (402 community-oncology MCL patients initiating a BTKi 2019-2021), not a national flow. No G-BA procedure for liso-cel in MCL as of the G-BA site listing. Existing E1a denominator: 3,500-3,800 new MCL cases per year (US). The label technically requires at least two prior lines including a BTKi, so MCL_2L is a misnomer inherited from the key list; it is a 3L+ population.

indication_label: Children 2 to 11 years of age with severe SCD (recurrent VOCs) or TDT newly eligible under the US paediatric label (SCD and TDT combined)

verbatim: The U.S. FDA recently approved CASGEVY in children 2 years of age and older with SCD or TDT, making it the first genetic therapy indicated for children as young as 2 years for both SCD and TDT. With this approval, achieved in just 53 days post filing, approximately 5,500 patients with SCD or TDT may be eligible for treatment with CASGEVY for the first time.
source_doc: Vertex 8-K Ex-99.1, Vertex Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results (3 Aug 2026), CASGEVY section
notes: US only: the sentence refers to the FDA approval; the 10-Q of 4 Aug 2026 repeats it verbatim ("Approximately 5,500 patients with SCD or TDT may be eligible for treatment with CASGEVY for the first time with this approval"). Vertex gives no SCD/TDT split. Duplicates the E2 row filed under SCD_VOC_12plus; re-keyed here to the new indication key.

indication_label: Children 2 to 11 with TDT newly eligible under the US paediatric label (share of the 5,500 combined figure)
verbatim: approximately 5,500 patients with SCD or TDT may be eligible for treatment with CASGEVY for the first time.
source_doc: Vertex 8-K Ex-99.1, Vertex Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results (3 Aug 2026), CASGEVY section

indication_label: Adultos con mieloma múltiple en recaída y refractario tras al menos una línea previa (IMiD y IP), progresión al último tratamiento y refractarios a lenalidomida
verbatim: La Comisión Interministerial de Precios de los Medicamentos, en su sesión de 26 de febrero de 2025, acordó proponer a la Dirección General de Cartera Común del SNS y Farmacia la inclusión en la prestación farmacéutica del SNS de este medicamento y su financiación para el tratamiento de pacientes adultos con mieloma múltiple en recaída y refractario que han recibido al menos una línea previa de tratamiento, incluidos un agente inmunomodulador y un inhibidor del proteasoma, han presentado progresión de la enfermedad al último tratamiento y son refractarios a lenalidomida.
source_doc: Ministerio de Sanidad, Informe público sobre la decisión de inclusión en la prestación farmacéutica de ciltacabtagén autoleucel (Carvykti) (26 May 2025); AEMPS IPT-339/V1/29012025 Carvykti (full text grepped)
notes: Neither the CIPM public report nor IPT-339 states an eligible or expected patient number; financing is under a pay-for-results agreement (PFS-based) within the Plan de Abordaje de las Terapias Avanzadas, with a protocolo farmacoclínico dated 1 Apr 2025 (https://www.sanidad.gob.es/areas/farmacia/infoMedicamentos/terapiasAvanzadas/docs/01042025_Protocolo_farmacoclinico_ciltacabtagen_autoleucel_mmrr_2l.pdf, not fetched). IPT-339 gives Spanish MM incidence 5.3-6.9 per 100,000 per year (2020) and 16,307 prevalent cases in 2020 (8,925 men, 7,382 women).

source_doc: Diariofarma, "Mieloma múltiple: los expertos, ilusionados con la llegada de Carvykti en segunda línea" (3 Apr 2025), as paraphrased in a search summary

indication_label: LBCL refractory to or relapsed within 12 months of first-line therapy and intended for autologous SCT (2L axi-cel eligible), US budget-impact model
unit: patients per 1,000,000 health-plan members per year
verbatim: It was estimated that 9 patients in a million member plan would be eligible for axi-cel treatment as 2L LBCL patients.
source_doc: Perales MA, Kuruvilla J, Snider JT, Vadgama S, Blissett R, El-Moustaid F, Smith NJ, Patel AR, Johnston PB. The Cost-Effectiveness of Axicabtagene Ciloleucel as Second-Line Therapy in Patients with Large B-Cell Lymphoma in the United States: An Economic Evaluation of the ZUMA-7 Trial. Transplant Cell Ther 2022;28(11):750.e1-750.e6 (doi 10.1016/j.jtct.2022.08.010)
notes: Kite-funded economic evaluation, but the method is published: BIM inputs table gives incidence of LBCL 54 per 1,000,000 (SEER), primary refractory disease 15% and relapsed disease 25% (Sehn 2021), proportion relapsed within 12 months 70% (Maurer 2014), proportion intended for auto-SCT 50% (Friedberg 2011); 54 x (0.15 + 0.25 x 0.70) x 0.50 = 8.8 per million. This is the independent (methods-stated) counterpart to the Kite boilerplate 5,400-7,200 in E1a.

indication_label: LBCL refractory to or relapsed within 12 months of first-line therapy, all-comers (US label population, no transplant-intent filter)
verbatim: Incidence of LBCL 54/1,000,000 ... SEER; Primary refractory disease 15% ... Sehn 2021; Relapsed disease 25% ... Sehn 2021; Proportion relapsed within 12 months 70% Maurer 2014; Proportion intended for auto-SCT 50% ... Friedberg 2011
source_doc: Derived from the Perales 2022 BIM inputs (SEER, Sehn 2021, Maurer 2014) and the US Census Bureau Vintage 2024 resident population
notes: Arithmetic: 54 per million x 340,110,988 US residents (1 July 2024) = 18,366 LBCL cases per year; early relapse/refractory share = 15% + 25% x 70% = 32.5%; 18,366 x 0.325 = 5,969 per year. The US label (Yescarta Apr 2022, Breyanzi Jun 2022) does not require transplant intent (Breyanzi also covers transplant-ineligible patients), so this is the label flow; the transplant-intended subset is 5,969 x 50% = 2,984 (or 9 per million x 340.1m = 3,061 using the paper rounding). Sits at the low end of the Kite boilerplate 5,400-7,200 range in E1a.
